meta.note: Editable QA cases for the release gate. Run: node release-management/qa/run-qa.js -> writes qa-result.json. Each case asserts a RULE still holds in the source, in plain English under why. kind: lint = source present/absent/count on PHP/JS (useful lint, NOT executed behavioral/PHP QA); governance = Hub wiring + JSON validity we can actually check here; manual = a human reminder, never fails the gate. Types: present/absent/count/json_ok. A /slashes/ needle is a regex. repo:warehouse cases skip (not fail) when the warehouse repo is absent. A release whose cases are only lint/manual reports LINT-ONLY, never PASS, because source lint cannot certify PHP/staging behavior (that comes from Codex + a PHP/staging run).

cases.title: ACID applies to Egypt and Kenya only
cases.why: The ACID Received / ACID Number / cargoX stage fields are required only for Egypt and Kenya. If this list changes, those fields would wrongly apply (or stop applying) to other countries.

cases.title: Blank country keeps the stage fields required (not N/A)
cases.why: A missing country must NOT silently make ACID fields N/A — it stays 'missing' so the field is still required and the user is told to set the country. Without this, a blank-country order could be shipped past a required ACID check.

cases.title: Blank country never maps straight to N/A
cases.why: Only a known non-ACID country becomes N/A; the blank case is handled before this line. Confirms the required/na decision runs after the blank guard.

cases.title: Unknown BL / bank doc type is 'missing', never N/A
cases.why: Only the two known values decide BL/bank state; anything else is 'missing' (still required), so an unrecognised doc type can't skip a required check.

cases.title: BUG-002: a future shipped date is blocked
cases.why: The shipped date is the day the shipment left, so it cannot be later than today. This is the guard that stops a future date (usually a wrong year) from being saved.

cases.title: BUG-002: an unreadable shipped date is blocked, not guessed
cases.needle: The shipped date could not be read
cases.why: A date that cannot be parsed is blocked with a clear message — it is never silently treated as today.

cases.title: BUG-002: no silent 'today' fallback for the shipped date
cases.needle: Please enter the shipped date (the day the shipment left). Nothing was saved.
cases.why: When no shipped date and no usable load date exist, the save is refused and the user is asked for the date — the code must not quietly stamp Carbon::now().

cases.title: BUG-002: a future load date can't stand in as the shipped date
cases.needle: The load date of this order is in the future, so it cannot be used as the shipped date
cases.why: If the shipped date is taken from the load date, a future load date must still be refused — the same future-date rule, applied to the fallback path.

cases.title: Inventory flow chart query is read-only
cases.why: The grade-flow chart only reads movement totals. It must never write to the database. This checks the gradeFlow method contains no insert/update/delete.

cases.title: Chart totals: inbound from scan-in weight, outbound from shipped date
cases.why: Outbound is grouped by the actual shipped date; inbound by the receipt weight. Confirms the chart still reads the agreed columns (Thirds USA should read ~16.08M in / ~15.84M out, Jun21–Nov26).

cases.title: REFERENCE: Thirds USA chart totals and no 1984 bar
cases.why: Human check on staging: Thirds USA inbound ~16,080,000 lb / outbound ~15,840,000 lb across Jun 2021–Nov 2026, with NO stray 1984 bar. Codex flagged (22 Nov 11:49) that the >18-month leading-gap drop removes legitimate old movement from 'all-time' totals — that fix is owned by the warehouse-skin session and must land before this item moves to production.

cases.title: BUG-001: empty-pallet unit is derived (pallets restored to Inventory Summary)
cases.why: Human check on staging: the ~2,685 pallets that had dropped out of the Inventory Summary are back, the unit derived from the skew number. Owned by the inventory session; this is a reminder, not a blocking source assertion.

cases.title: Hub: Change Schedule tab is permission-gated
cases.why: Only super admin (handled earlier) and anyone given releases.access can see the Change Schedule tab. Without this gate the release register would be visible to everyone.

cases.title: Hub: the /api/releases route is GET-only (no writes)
cases.why: The release register is read-only to the Hub. The screen must never be able to deploy or edit; only GET exists.

cases.title: Hub: releases.access permission exists in Settings
cases.why: Max can only grant the Change Schedule tab if the permission key is wired into Settings.

cases.title: Hub: NT Warehouse panel carries no Hub token
cases.why: The in-Hub warehouse panel is a plain iframe of the live warehouse with no Hub session/profile/token passed across origins (XF).

cases.title: Hub: version badge is current
cases.why: House rule: the visible version badge is bumped every build so Max can tell which build is live.

cases.title: Governance: the release register is valid JSON
cases.why: The Change Schedule screen and the deploy scripts both read this file. A bad hand-edit must be caught here before it blanks the screen.
